text: Who can assure me that Vulkan is the future? This is the key to pick the right decision between buying 1060 or 480...
author: @fitman84

text:
I expect Vulkan to gain support & do well in general, but DX12 will be the more commonly supported API.  Although RX 480 seems to have more of an edge in Vulkan than in DX12, we don't have lots of Vulkan games to test with now.  Even if Vulkan totally flopped (which I'm pretty sure it won't), the RX480 is still a better card in general for well-optimized DX12 games.  Low-level async APIs are the future without question.

GTX 1060 vs RX 480 is really about where you put your emphasis: performance in DX<=11, or performance in DX12 (& Vulkan).  If you plan to keep the card for a few years I think RX 480 is probably a better choice, but if you're playing lots of GTA V for example it would be perfectly valid to go for the 1060.  If you want variable sync, FreeSync is a much better value proposition than G-sync.  No matter what, you won't be making a grievous error by buying either of these (just get a decent AIB card & not reference/FE).
